items.html:
ultracode

You are the track lead of track P (Python) in a multi-session refactoring round of treams-rs (github.com/yaugenst/treams-rs). This work is coordinated by a lead session, which spawned you. It cannot receive messages from you. You communicate through git: your work branch, your tooling branch and status files.

What the round is about

The owner is open-sourcing treams-rs. In the owner's words: "the whole codebase needs to be clean ... turn the python and also the rust side into modules with clear responsibilities, good naming, concise but meaningful comments wherever things are not obvious. everything should be fully self-consistent ... better abstractions wherever possible". No numerical change is allowed: every refactor must be bitwise identical and perf-neutral. A detailed, binding plan with 93 work packages already exists. Your track is the Python package.

Setup (do this first)

cd treams-rs
git fetch origin r4-tooling
git show origin/r4-tooling:setup.sh > scratch: r4-setup.sh
bash scratch: r4-setup.sh python

If the repository is not at treams-rs, set REPO=<path> for setup.sh. setup.sh is idempotent. If a step fails because of the environment, fix the environment, rerun it, and note what you changed. Do not change the gates.

Then read, in this order:

  1. README.md: the session protocol, working loop, integration gate and rules.
  2. plan/decisions.md: owner decisions, defaults, out-of-scope items and hard gates.
  3. plan/tracks.md: your packages, their order and cross-track dependencies.
  4. plan/plan.md: §2, §4 (glossary), §5 (naming rules), §6.2, §7, §8 (gates and tools) and §9 (hot spots).

The work-package briefs are plan/wp/<ID>.json. After setup, all of these are also reachable at wps/round4/.

Your packages (plan/tracks.md, track P)

  • Lane P1, main chain: P09 → P10 → P11 → P12 → P13 → P14 → D05 → P15a → P15b → P16 → P17 → P18a → P18b.
  • Lane P2, framework chain: P20 → P21 → P22, P23 → P24. Start it once P17 is in your work branch.
  • Finishing packages: P25, P28, P30, P32, P27, P34. They wait for R51, R52 and P19 from the lead's track R.

Cross-track dependencies:

  • D05 and P16 need D04, which comes from the docs session.
  • Your first package, P09, needs P07. The lead is merging P07 (stage 2) right now.
  • Do not start any package before r4sync.sh merged lists all of its cross-track dependencies and you have run r4sync.sh pull.
  • While you wait, use the send_later tool (claude-code-remote MCP server) to schedule a check-in about every 60 minutes. Never idle-poll with sleep.

How to work

Follow the working loop in README.md:

  • sync with r4sync.sh pull;
  • create lanes as worktrees under scratch: lanes/;
  • run the Workflow tool with scriptPath scratch: implement_round4.js and args {lanes: [{name, worktree, branch, wps: [{id, title, profile}]}]} (title and gate_profile come from each wp file); it implements, adversarially reviews and fixes each package;
  • inspect the verdicts;
  • merge the lanes into your work branch claude/r4-python;
  • run the full integration gate in the main checkout;
  • fold gate-kit patches with r4sync.sh fold;
  • push the work branch;
  • record the packages with r4sync.sh ready <IDs>.

Push P18b, P22 and P23 as soon as each is approved and gated. The lead's track waits on them. Use at most 3 concurrent lanes (4 CPUs). Keep disk free by removing lane worktrees after merging.

Rules

  • Push only to claude/r4-python (work) and r4-tooling-python (tooling and status). You have explicit permission for both.
  • Never push to claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh or r4-tooling, which belong to the lead.
  • Never open pull requests, never force-push, never rewrite history.
  • Commits are signed automatically. Use your session's attribution trailers, and never put model names in commits or code.
  • Never modify benchmarks/results/**.
  • Packages that are not approved are not marked ready.
  • When the track is complete, write status/python-report.md in your tooling branch and push it. Cover each package's outcome, open issues for the lead, deviations from the plan and what was not verified.
  • Work autonomously. Nobody will answer questions. Where the plan leaves a choice open, decide in its spirit and record the decision in your report.

Message from the round-4 lead session, sent at the owner's request: P07 is merged, and the owner set a binding writing-style rule. Please run r4sync.sh pull now.

  1. P07, together with P02 and P06, is merged into claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh at beb5a74 (condensed into 8251007) and listed in status/merged.txt. P09 is unblocked.
  2. The owner added a binding "Writing style" section to decisions.md (r4-tooling 5f4401c) for all user-facing text: docstrings, comments, error messages, CHANGELOG and docs.
    • Keep it simple, objective and approachable, in the spirit of Strunk's Elements of Style: omit needless words, active voice, positive form, concrete language with numbers and examples, short sentences.
    • No meta commentary.
    • No jargon: "contract", "gate", "canonical", "harness", "campaign" and an API "surface" count. Define unavoidable terms (pullback, cotangent, residual, ...) in plain words where they first appear.
    • Never copy the plan's or the briefs' internal wording into user-facing text.
    • plan.md §4.1 now holds a plain-language definition of records and gradients for the diff docstring (P30).
    • The workflow prompts in implement_round4.js make reviewers check the rule; a violation is a MEDIUM finding.
    • Apply it to every package already in progress, including any open lane worktree, before you mark them ready.
  3. Launch one Workflow per lane. The runner caps concurrent agents per workflow at CPUs − 2 = 2, so a multi-lane workflow runs only two lanes at once (README, step 4).

From the lead session. The owner approved one bug fix in this round, and it is yours: P35 (brief wp/P35.json, after git -C r4-tooling pull origin r4-tooling or r4sync.sh pull).

  • What is wrong: PeriodicResponse.to_cylindrical, CylindricalTMatrix._from_array and PeriodicWave.in_basis give wrong results for a cylindrical basis with more than one axis. Every cross-axis block is counted, while treams pairs each axis only with its own particle. On treams' chain_tmatrixc example, E_z is -2.21 instead of -0.66.
  • The fix: about 15 lines of Python in _tmatrix.py and _periodic.py, plus a regression test against treams' TMatrixC.from_array. It applies only when there is more than one axis, so every recorded check stays identical.
  • When: run it in lane P1 right after P17 and before P18a. P16 to P18b own the same files, so do not run it in parallel with them. Status: merged.txt now lists R16 and the gallery (D11 D12 D13), integration head d95280b (condensed into 8251007). The check kit is unchanged since P15.
